{"episodes":[{"ep":4,"title":"One Workshop","script":"SFX: Printing press slams. Type rattles across a stone floor.
EWAN: Stop the press. Lock the door.
ADA: That costs money. Tell me why.
EWAN: Serial B-417 was sold in Glasgow. Tonight, a farmer gave me the same number in Edinburgh.
SFX: Press wheel slows to a groaning stop.
MASTER PRINTER: Miss Wren, your father gave no order to stop.
ADA: Then charge the lost sheet to me.
MASTER PRINTER: You do not own an account here.
ADA: One day I shall own the press. Leave us.
MASTER PRINTER: A woman owning a print room. Shall I set that in fairy type?
ADA: Set it in twelve-point and spell my name correctly.
SFX: Door closes. Key turns.
EWAN: I need the banknote plate.
ADA: No.
EWAN: Families are buying notes that cannot be redeemed.
ADA: And if my father finds you touching his plates, I lose my place before I ever own one.
EWAN: Gregor has my mother's debt ledger. I cannot walk away. I need proof strong enough to break his hold.
ADA: Proof will not pay your mother's arrears.
EWAN: Neither will a banknote printed twice under one serial number.
SFX: Paper unfolds against a worktable.
ADA: B-417. The numbering wheel should advance after every impression.
EWAN: Could it slip backwards?
ADA: Once, perhaps. Not from Glasgow to Edinburgh. Someone reset it.
EWAN: Why?
ADA: Because they printed another run and wanted the first buyer to think his note belonged to a limited issue.
EWAN: How many runs?
ADA: Bring me one of each document from the Briarhaven office.
EWAN: Gregor keeps the charter cabinet locked.
ADA: You engraved his seal in a morning. Do not become honest at the least useful moment.
SFX: Metal picks scrape inside a lock.
NARRATOR: Before midnight, Ewan returned with a constitution, a bank charter, a military commission and the note numbered B-417.
SFX: Print-room shutters knock. A lamp wick hisses.
ADA: Constitution first. Hold the lower edge.
EWAN: There is a crescent in the paper.
ADA: A flaw in the mould. Same crescent here on the bank charter.
EWAN: And on the commission.
ADA: Three institutions are buying from the same paper maker. That proves economy, not fraud.
EWAN: The ink cured on the same day.
ADA: Then we test the plates.
SFX: Drawer slides open. Heavy copper lands on wood.
EWAN: That is the Green Cross from the royal seal.
ADA: Listen.
SFX: Thin paper laid over copper. Charcoal rubs rapidly.
ADA: The left arm has a nick. Small as a pin bite.
EWAN: The constitution's royal seal has it.
ADA: So does the bank charter.
EWAN: The military commission too.
ADA: Separate offices could order the same emblem.
EWAN: Not the same damaged plate.
ADA: Correct. Now the border.
SFX: Second copper plate scrapes onto the table.
EWAN: Laurel leaves, crown, two ships.
ADA: Count the leaves beside the crown.
EWAN: Eleven.
ADA: The banknote has eleven. The land grant has eleven. The constitution has eleven.
EWAN: Parliament, bank and royal office.
ADA: All struck from plates cut in this room.
SFX: Nothing. Long.
EWAN: Say it plainly.
ADA: Briarhaven's government is a print order. Its parliament, bank and royal seal are physically manufactured in one Edinburgh workshop.
EWAN: Then the mystery is finished.
ADA: No. The mystery is why my father accepted the orders.
EWAN: Gregor paid him.
ADA: Gregor pays in promises. My father prefers coin.
EWAN: Who brought the designs?
ADA: A messenger. Gloves, military posture, no name. Every order was entered under a different customer.
EWAN: Show me the order book.
ADA: No.
EWAN: Ada—
ADA: The book belongs to my father. If you take it, Gregor knows where the evidence came from. If he knows, this shop closes.
EWAN: It is already producing false government papers.
ADA: It is also feeding six compositors, two apprentices and my father. Facts do not become simple because you are frightened.
EWAN: I am ashamed, not frightened.
ADA: You are both.
SFX: Numbering wheel clicks.
ADA: Here. B-417.
EWAN: The wheel has been fixed at that number.
ADA: It was not an accident. Every sheet in the second run carried B-417 until the operator advanced it by hand.
EWAN: How many sheets?
ADA: The press tally says five hundred.
EWAN: Five hundred duplicate notes.
ADA: Worth one pound each to the families. Worth paper and ink to the people selling them.
EWAN: I will take the tally.
ADA: You will take nothing that names this shop.
EWAN: Then Gregor continues.
ADA: If you confront him with paper, he burns paper. You need something he cannot call a clerk's mistake.
EWAN: The damaged plate.
ADA: The original would be missed before breakfast.
EWAN: Can you strike an impression?
ADA: An impression can be dismissed as a copy.
EWAN: Then make me a duplicate.
ADA: Copper costs fourteen shillings. Engraving it costs a night. Discovery costs me everything.
EWAN: I have three shillings.
ADA: Keep them. Poverty is not persuasive when we are discussing mine.
EWAN: What do you want?
ADA: When this breaks, you say publicly that I found it. Not you. Not some banker. Me.
EWAN: You want your name tied to a fraud.
ADA: I want my skill tied to its exposure. Men forgive skill after they have finished condemning the woman who used it.
EWAN: You have my word.
ADA: Your word is printed on sixty acres that do not exist.
EWAN: Then take the only thing I have not sold. My name.
ADA: Your name is already on the certificates.
EWAN: Exactly.
SFX: Engraving tool bites into copper.
NARRATOR: For four hours, Ada copied every nick, leaf and false symbol. Ewan worked the bellows and listened for footsteps.
SFX: Distant church bell strikes four. Engraving stops.
EWAN: If Gregor discovers this—
ADA: He will be courteous. That is when he is most dangerous.
SFX: Fist pounds on the street door.
MASTER PRINTER: Ada! Open this door!
ADA: He is early.
EWAN: Hide the plate.
MASTER PRINTER: I have the constable with me!
ADA: The constable drinks with my father. That is not the same as law.
EWAN: Come with me.
ADA: Through the paper hatch. You first.
EWAN: I will not leave you.
ADA: Then we are both caught, and Gregor keeps printing.
SFX: Door shudders under another blow.
MASTER PRINTER: Open now!
ADA: Ewan, when you hear the bolt, run.
EWAN: And tomorrow?
ADA: Come when the shop opens.
SFX: Small metal plate wrapped in cloth.
ADA: Take the duplicate plate, Ewan.
NARRATOR: The next morning, her father's print shop had been emptied.
NARRATOR: Ada had vanished."},{"ep":5,"title":"Two Hundred Thousand Pounds","script":"SFX: Bare shelves echo. A loose shop bell rattles.
EWAN: Where is Ada Wren?
MASTER PRINTER: There is no printer by that name here.
EWAN: This shop was full yesterday.
MASTER PRINTER: Then yesterday is the address you require.
SFX: Coins slapped onto a counter.
EWAN: Tell me where they took her.
MASTER PRINTER: Keep your three shillings. You may shortly need them for your own journey.
EWAN: Did Gregor empty this place?
MASTER PRINTER: A gentleman settled my liabilities. I have been advised not to burden him with gratitude.
SFX: Shop door opens sharply.
MESSENGER: Ewan Pell?
EWAN: Who is asking?
MESSENGER: Briarhaven Finance Office. London. You are required before the loan presentation at noon tomorrow.
EWAN: Required by whom?
MESSENGER: Mr Cyrus Perring. The Northhaven settler manifest closes at four.
EWAN: What has a loan presentation to do with a settler ship?
MESSENGER: I carry invitations, not answers.
SFX: Invitation card tears in Ewan's hand.
NARRATOR: Ewan went to London with Ada's copper plate under his shirt and the duplicate banknote in his pocket.
SFX: Auction bell rings. A crowded banking hall murmurs.
COMPERE: Gentlemen, subscribers and representatives of the press. The Briarhaven national loan is fixed at two hundred thousand pounds.
SFX: Applause swells.
CYRUS: Mr Pell. You are late.
EWAN: I did not agree to prepare a loan.
CYRUS: Agreement is a sentimental word for employment. Stand beside the certificate table.
EWAN: What assets secure the bonds?
CYRUS: Land, customs, mineral revenues and the future prosperity of a nation.
EWAN: Which customs house collected the revenue?
CYRUS: Investors do not purchase yesterday, Mr Pell. They purchase tomorrow.
EWAN: I need the treasury accounts.
CYRUS: You need a clean pen.
SFX: Walking stick taps twice.
GREGOR: Our clerk has arrived. Do proceed.
EWAN: I require one answer before I put my name on any bond. Where is Ada Wren?
GREGOR: Miss Wren's domestic arrangements are not a banking matter.
EWAN: Her father's shop was emptied overnight.
GREGOR: Then he has discovered efficiency. You should congratulate him.
EWAN: I will not prepare these certificates.
GREGOR: Your mother's shop is on leased ground, is it not.
EWAN: Do not speak of her here.
GREGOR: Quite right. Family debts are private. Public defaults are so much uglier.
CYRUS: We have journalists waiting.
GREGOR: Mr Pell will perform his duty. He has a gift for recovering from hesitation.
COMPERE: Mr Perring, may the market understand that your bank has examined the security?
CYRUS: It may understand precisely this: after review of the submitted instruments, I validate the issue of a Briarhaven loan in the principal amount of two hundred thousand pounds.
SFX: Louder applause. Pens scratch across reporters' notebooks.
VOICE IN CROWD: Perring validates it!
SECOND VOICE: Put me down for five hundred!
EWAN: You have not named a single asset.
CYRUS: I named the submitted instruments.
EWAN: A constitution printed in Edinburgh. A bank charter from the same room. A seal made from the same plate.
GREGOR: Careful. An incompetent clerk questioning a banker before subscribers may sound like envy.
CYRUS: Mr Pell, do you possess evidence suitable for this room?
SFX: Ewan touches cloth-wrapped metal beneath his coat.
EWAN: Not yet.
CYRUS: Then this room possesses more evidence than you do.
COMPERE: Subscription books are open!
SFX: Crowd surges toward desks.
SILAS: Pell, move. You are blocking money.
EWAN: Silas, what price are you quoting?
SILAS: Issue price is eighty. First resale is already eighty-six.
EWAN: The certificates do not exist.
SILAS: That is why they are light enough to rise.
EWAN: People are paying above issue price for unprinted bonds?
SILAS: Six pounds profit before luncheon. Nobody asks a harbour to interrupt that.
EWAN: You knew there was no harbour.
SILAS: I know there is no harbour account in the papers sent to London. Those are different statements, especially in court.
EWAN: How many certificates has Cyrus promised?
SILAS: Two thousand at one hundred pounds principal. Four hundred are subscribed. Another three hundred reserved.
EWAN: And I am expected to make them real.
SILAS: You are expected to make them rectangular.
SFX: Ledger closes.
GREGOR: Mr Pell, the certificate room.
EWAN: No.
GREGOR: I admire a man who chooses principle after his mother's roof has entered the discussion.
EWAN: If I print them, I want access to every supporting paper.
CYRUS: An unusual condition from a junior clerk.
EWAN: Your validation is public. My work will be public. Give me the maps, harbour accounts, official appointments and capital expenditure schedules.
CYRUS: Give him the submission box.
GREGOR: Cyrus—
CYRUS: If our instruments are sound, examination improves them.
GREGOR: Naturally. Mr Pell may inspect everything.
SFX: Iron box unlocks.
NARRATOR: For six hours, Ewan numbered bond certificates while subscribers paid deposits in the next room.
SFX: Pen scratches. Numbering stamp thumps repeatedly.
EWAN: Certificate 311. No harbour account.
SILAS: Stamp it.
EWAN: Certificate 312. No construction payroll.
SILAS: Stamp it.
EWAN: No customs officers, no magistrates, no warehouse leases.
SILAS: The market closes at five. Misery can continue afterward.
EWAN: Here is the capital map.
SFX: Large paper spreads.
SILAS: Very green.
EWAN: Parliament House, Royal Bank, military barracks, hospital, cathedral, three paved squares.
SILAS: Thomas writes attractively.
EWAN: There are no surveyor's coordinates. No builder. No dates. This is an illustration.
SILAS: It was coloured by hand. Investors appreciate labour.
EWAN: The first settlers are on the Northhaven manifest.
SILAS: One hundred and seventy-three passengers. Thirty-eight children. Departure at four tomorrow afternoon.
EWAN: Why did you not tell me?
SILAS: You did not ask for shipping. You asked for bonds.
EWAN: They are sailing toward a capital supported by no expenditure at all.
SILAS: They purchased land, appointments and banknotes. Hope was included without charge.
EWAN: Help me stop the ship.
SILAS: At eighty-six, I am earning six pounds per bond. At four o'clock tomorrow, I expect eighty-nine. That is my answer.
EWAN: When these families return, they will name everyone in this room.
SILAS: If they return, I shall reconsider.
SFX: Chair scrapes back.
EWAN: I am taking copies of the missing accounts.
SILAS: Copies of nothing are still nothing.
EWAN: Then I will send nothing with official signatures attached.
NARRATOR: By dawn, Ewan had assembled the empty harbour account, the unsigned building schedule and the list of government posts with no officials appointed to them.
SFX: Rain on carriage roof. Hooves hammer a road.
EWAN: Faster!
DRIVER: The horse has one speed left, sir, and you are spending it!
EWAN: Northhaven harbour. The settler quay.
SFX: Distant ship bell rings twice.
EWAN: That bell—how far?
DRIVER: Half a mile.
EWAN: Take the lane by the warehouses.
DRIVER: Gates will be shut.
EWAN: Break the gate.
DRIVER: With whose carriage?
EWAN: Mine if we reach the quay. Gregor's if we do not.
SFX: Hooves accelerate. Wooden gate splinters.
EWAN: Harbour master! Hold the Briarhaven vessel!
HARBOUR VOICE: She has cleared the wall!
SFX: Ewan runs over wet stone. Papers slap in his hand.
EWAN: Signal her! I have proof from the loan box!
HARBOUR VOICE: What proof?
EWAN: No harbour expenditure. No buildings. No appointed officials. The promised capital is not there!
SFX: Ship's departure cannon fires across the water.
NARRATOR: The first ship carrying settlers sailed before Ewan could send proof that the promised capital had no harbour, buildings or officials."},{"ep":6,"title":"The Promised Capital","script":"SFX: Gangplank chains clatter against a crowded quay.
PURser: Name for the southbound coastal packet?
EWAN: Elias Bell.
PURser: Occupation?
EWAN: Accounts clerk.
PURser: Papers?
EWAN: Paid passage and one trunk.
PURser: That is money, Mr Bell. I asked for papers.
EWAN: The ship that just sailed carried one hundred and seventy-three people on false papers. Mine should trouble you less.
PURser: People who trouble me pay double.
SFX: Coins counted into a palm.
PURser: Welcome aboard, Mr Bell.
SFX: Gangplank lifted. Packet whistle shrieks.
NARRATOR: Ewan took the coastal packet south under a false name, transferred to a mail brig in London, and spent six weeks crossing with Ada's plate wrapped beneath his spare shirt.
SFX: Surf crashes against a small boat. Oars knock in wooden locks.
BOATMAN: Sable Coast ahead. No dock at your landing.
EWAN: The map marks a stone harbour.
BOATMAN: Then ask the map to tie the boat.
EWAN: There should be a capital beyond the river mouth.
BOATMAN: There is jungle beyond the river mouth.
SFX: Boat grinds onto shingle.
INES: Stay in the boat.
EWAN: Are you the interpreter from Crownwater Colony?
INES: Who asks?
EWAN: Elias Bell.
INES: No. Elias Bell keeps his eyes on his own boots. You counted the shoreline twice and the crates three times. Clerk's habit.
EWAN: Ewan Pell.
INES: The name on the Briarhaven certificates.
EWAN: You have seen them?
INES: Seven months ago, two men came with a land grant and muskets. Last month, another came with a customs appointment. All three expected me to salute.
EWAN: Did any Briarhaven official receive them?
INES: You are speaking to the person who sent them back alive.
EWAN: A settler ship is coming. Thirty-eight children are aboard.
INES: Then turn around and warn it.
EWAN: I tried before it sailed.
INES: Try from the sea.
EWAN: My packet is gone. I need to see the capital and carry proof to the authorities.
INES: You need water, boots and permission to cross land that your map gives away without asking.
EWAN: Whose permission?
INES: Not Gregor Vale's.
EWAN: Can you take me there?
INES: No.
EWAN: I can pay.
INES: Men with paper countries always offer payment after they arrive on somebody else's shore.
EWAN: Then name what you want.
INES: Every document you carry. I read them first.
EWAN: The copper plate stays with me.
INES: Then the jungle stays between you and the capital.
EWAN: If you take it, I lose the only proof Ada left.
INES: Ada is a person?
EWAN: A printer. She found that the constitution, bank and royal seal came from one Edinburgh room. Then she vanished.
INES: And you came here instead of finding her.
EWAN: I came because one hundred and seventy-three settlers are following this route.
INES: That answer is nearly good enough.
SFX: Cloth unwraps. Copper rings beneath a fingernail.
INES: Eleven laurel leaves. The grants I saw had the same border.
EWAN: Will you guide me now?
INES: I will guide you until you lie. After that, the insects may have you.
SFX: Machete cuts thick growth. Boots sink into mud.
NARRATOR: On the first day, the road printed on Ewan's map took them into a mangrove channel and ended underwater.
EWAN: The guidebook calls this King's Avenue.
INES: Does it mention the crocodiles?
EWAN: It says carriages travel four abreast.
INES: Four crocodiles could.
EWAN: The capital is marked three miles inland.
INES: We have walked five.
EWAN: There should be milestones.
INES: There should be honesty. Walk.
SFX: Insects pulse. A boot tears free from deep mud.
EWAN: Wait. I hear stone shifting.
INES: That is not stone.
SFX: Rotten timber collapses.
EWAN: A roof beam.
INES: An abandoned trading shelter.
EWAN: The map labels this Government House.
INES: It had one room. Traders stored salt here before the fever years.
EWAN: Parliament House should stand east of it.
INES: East is swamp.
EWAN: The barracks?
INES: Termite mounds.
EWAN: Hospital?
INES: Nothing.
EWAN: Cathedral?
INES: Trees.
SFX: Ewan tears a page from the guidebook.
INES: Do not throw it down. The jungle did not print the lie.
EWAN: I prepared certificates naming streets that were never built.
INES: Then remember the names. Survivors may ask who sold them.
EWAN: I did not sell the land.
INES: Your signature did.
EWAN: Gregor forced me.
INES: That may matter in Edinburgh. It will not make a roof here.
SFX: Distant thunder rolls.
EWAN: How long before the settler ship arrives?
INES: If winds favour them, ten days. If not, twenty. If fever boards first, longer.
EWAN: We need shelter for one hundred and seventy-three.
INES: There is shelter for twelve at the old post, if the roof holds.
EWAN: Food?
INES: Not for a ship. Local villages will not empty their stores because strangers bought imaginary farms.
EWAN: Fresh water?
INES: Two wells. One turns brackish after heavy rain.
EWAN: Then we warn Crownwater Colony and bring supplies.
INES: The nearest official post is four days by boat.
EWAN: Take me.
INES: The storm arrives tonight. The river may close.
EWAN: There must be a signal station.
INES: On your map?
EWAN: Yes.
INES: Ask it for a lantern.
SFX: First heavy raindrops strike broad leaves.
NARRATOR: On the second day, Ines led Ewan past the last marked street and into ground the Briarhaven map left blank.
SFX: Rainwater pours from trees. Machete stops.
INES: Do not move.
EWAN: Snake?
INES: Cut stone.
SFX: Mud scraped with a blade.
EWAN: A boundary marker.
INES: Read the face.
EWAN: The letters are worn. B... R... I...
INES: Briarhaven.
EWAN: That cannot be here.
INES: Copper plate in Edinburgh. Carved stone here. Your paper country prepared more than one kind of evidence.
EWAN: The lower line is buried.
SFX: Hands dig rapidly through wet earth.
INES: There is a date.
EWAN: Eighteen thirty-one.
INES: When does Gregor claim he first received this territory?
EWAN: Three years later.
SFX: Rain strikes exposed stone.
INES: This Briarhaven boundary marker is dated 1831.
INES: Three years before Gregor claims he first received the territory."}],"beat_sheet":[{"beat_id":"b012","ep":4,"seq":1,"world_time":"1834-04-12","location":"Wren print shop,
